rv.q: An exhilarating reading that reframes the psychological landscape of the original for our own image-obsessed age.
This is an unsparing depiction of a world in which everyone uses everyone, nothing is quite what it seems and no one is completely sure who they are. It is Joe and Norma’s world, and it’s also ours.
After this soul-baring, roof-raising performance it would be churlish to disagree.
It's a tour de force of a show, in love with showbiz and the creation and destruction of illusions.
As a piece of live theatre this is truly awesome stuff.
It’s the kind of uncompromisingly brilliant performance that makes you want to use cliches like “tour de force”.

There is a magnificence in simplicity, and Scherzinger’s Norma, initially drawing herself regally downstage, in black dress and shades, her dark hair long with a soupcon of the untamed warrior, has a poise that thrills.
This frisky, occasionally bonkers production easily exceeded my expectations for an evening watching a histrionic Lloyd Webber musical.
Genre swamps character: it is a dazzling argument, but more hologram than heart.
So why, with all these riches, does it leave this critic so removed and restless?
Endlessly fierce and hip, this bold interpretation of the material dazzles with its transformation of the musical’s bare bones into a tragic feast of profound power.
This is a Sunset Boulevard for a new generation.
Lloyd’s streamlined approach has a power of its own.
It’s an extraordinary performance in a beautiful rethinking of one of Lloyd Webber’s greatest shows.
Nicole Scherzinger has a great vocal range and is not afraid to make harsh sounds when they fit the drama.
Even without the considerable ingenuity of the director, the former Pussycat Doll is primed to blow anybody's socks off.
By the end, for all its technical dazzlement, you’re left thinking, have we been watching “Sunset Boulevard” or “Everybody’s Talking About Jamie Lloyd”?
Overall the show feels like a Gothic opera staged in an underground car park during a blackout.
Norma’s back at last where she was born to be on the West End stage, and we wish she really was staying for good.

Jamie Lloyd's production of Sunset Boulevard is a radical masterpiece, with an impeccable cast, that will leave you stunned, astonished, and reeling as you leave the theatre, knowing that you've never seen anything quite like it.
The whole thing is quite simply phenomenal.
No matter if you have seen this show before.
There’s more than enough to make this a truly epic piece of theatre.
Sunset Boulevard never really gels as a whole.
Nicole Scherzinger Soars in Sunset Boulevard Revival

This production is unique, exciting, and stretches the boundaries of what we believe can be achieved in theatre, Lloyd has long been producing ground-breaking theatre, and this is nothing short of ground-breaking.
It’s a bravura moment in a show that left me shaken and stunned.
There are few things more thrilling in the theatre than watching something you know well being completely transformed before your eyes, and Jamie Lloyd’s Sunset Boulevard is truly thrilling.
Scherzinger was brilliant but miscast, the show needs a completely new score but that its direction was definitely worthy of a US audience.

cn.t: Critics hail Jamie Lloyd's radical, stripped-back reimagining as visually stunning and audacious, with Nicole Scherzinger delivering a career-defining performance, though some find the stark approach doesn't fully cohere.
